scheme_name: National Mission on Edible Oil–Oil Palm: Maintenance and Input Cost for Intercropping in Oilpalm
description:
The National Mission on Edible Oil–Oil Palm was launched in August 2021 by the Government of India. 

This initiative aims to reduce the country's dependence on imported edible oils. 

India is one of the largest consumers of edible oils globally, with imports accounting for nearly 60 percent of its total consumption. 

The mission is part of a broader strategy to enhance domestic production of edible oils. 

The primary objective of this mission is to increase the area under oil palm cultivation. 

The government aims to bring an additional 6.5 lakh hectares under oil palm cultivation by 2025-26. 

This initiative is expected to boost the production of crude palm oil. 

The target is to achieve a production of 10 lakh metric tonnes of crude palm oil by 2025-26. 

The scheme also focuses on providing financial assistance for maintenance and input costs associated with intercropping in oil palm cultivation. 

Farmers engaged in oil palm cultivation can receive support for intercropping with other crops. 

The intercropping is designed to provide additional income to farmers during the initial years of oil palm growth. 

The financial assistance covers various aspects including seeds, fertilizers, and other necessary inputs. 

Farmers can receive up to ₹30,000 per hectare for maintenance costs in the initial years. 

The assistance is provided for a period of up to five years. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of sustainable agricultural practices. 

It encourages farmers to adopt eco-friendly methods in oil palm cultivation. 

The eligibility criteria for farmers to participate in this scheme are specific. 

Farmers must be residents of India. 

They should have a minimum of 1 hectare of land for oil palm cultivation. 

The age limit for applicants is generally set at 18 years and above. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required for farmers to apply. 

However, they must demonstrate an understanding of oil palm cultivation practices. 

The application process involves several steps. 

Farmers must first register with the local agricultural department. 

They need to fill out an application form detailing their land ownership and cultivation plans. 

Required documents include proof of land ownership, identity proof, and bank account details. 

Once the application is submitted, it is verified by the local agricultural officer. 

After verification, eligible farmers are provided with a sanction order for financial assistance. 

The disbursement of funds is typically done through direct bank transfers. 

Farmers can expect to receive the first installment shortly after the sanction order is issued. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the progress of cultivation and adherence to guidelines. 

The timeline for application submission generally aligns with the agricultural calendar. 

Farmers are encouraged to apply during the pre-sowing season to ensure timely support. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The National Mission on Edible Oil–Oil Palm is overseen by the Department of Agriculture, Cooperation, and Farmers' Welfare. 

State governments play a crucial role in the implementation of the scheme. 

They are responsible for local outreach and support to farmers. 

The scheme is also supported by various agricultural universities and research institutions. 

These institutions provide technical assistance and training to farmers. 

The mission aims to create a robust supply chain for oil palm cultivation. 

This includes establishing processing units for crude palm oil. 

The government has also proposed incentives for private investment in oil palm processing. 

The expected outcome of the mission is significant. 

It aims to reduce the import dependency on edible oils by 10 percent by 2025-26. 

This would translate to savings of approximately ₹33,000 crores annually in foreign exchange. 

The mission also aims to create employment opportunities in rural areas. 

It is estimated that around 2.5 lakh jobs could be generated through this initiative. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from various stakeholders. 

Farmers have expressed optimism about the potential for increased income. 

The government has also launched awareness campaigns to educate farmers about oil palm cultivation. 

These campaigns focus on the benefits of oil palm as a cash crop. 

The mission aligns with the broader goals of the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative. 

It emphasizes self-reliance in agricultural production. 

The government is committed to providing continuous support to farmers under this scheme. 

Regular monitoring and evaluation of the program are conducted to assess its impact. 

The mission is expected to contribute significantly to the agricultural economy of India. 

It aims to enhance food security by increasing domestic oil production. 

The National Mission on Edible Oil–Oil Palm is a pivotal step towards achieving self-sufficiency in edible oils. 

Farmers are encouraged to participate actively in this transformative initiative. 

The government continues to refine the scheme based on feedback from the ground. 

This ensures that the support provided meets the actual needs of the farmers. 

The mission is a comprehensive approach to addressing the challenges of edible oil production in India. 

It combines financial assistance with technical support and capacity building. 

The long-term vision of the mission is to establish India as a leading producer of edible oils. 

This will not only benefit farmers but also contribute to the overall economic growth of the country. 

The National Mission on Edible Oil–Oil Palm represents a significant investment in the future of Indian agriculture. 

It is a proactive measure to ensure that the agricultural sector remains resilient and sustainable. 

The government remains committed to monitoring the progress of this mission closely. 

This will help in making necessary adjustments to enhance its effectiveness. 

Overall the mission is poised to make a lasting impact on India's agricultural landscape.
